points.text: Intent-perception score measures representation stability, averaged over trivial early layers

Different models used for analysis and ASR; explanation not tested on target models
PCA argument read from 2-D plot without quantitative measure or probe
PCA ordering does not exclude alternatives like readability or prompt length
Analysed layers chosen by citation, not validated on this model
Weak-OOD phenomenon based on small samples without CIs or repeated runs
GPT-4o serves as both target model and judge
Perturbation axes not comparable and grid points few
Some plotted ranges hard to read
'Universal' trend claim stronger than evidence

LLM judge only; no human validation or judge-sensitivity analysis
Defences such as input filtering or safety-tuned VLMs not tested

Contradictory shuffle results explained post hoc
JOCR success circularly taken as validation; weak-OOD analysis not applied to JOCR
Citation errors and wrong equation references
Ethics statement irrelevant; no dual-use or disclosure discussion

No defence or alignment recommendation despite stated goal
Theory heuristic; latent assumptions debated; evidence correlational not causal

GPT-4o judge may introduce bias
JOCR novelty limited: typography plus stochastic perturbation
Defences not explored

Pre-training/alignment mismatch hypothesis not new (mismatched generalization)
Weak-OOD phenomenon already observed empirically in JOOD
JOCR lacks principled procedure to generate weak-OOD inputs; intent preservation not guaranteed
Typos
Averaging layer-wise similarities ignores layer heterogeneity
No ablation of perturbation settings' effect on intent perception and refusal
